title: Michael Carrick uncertain of Matthijs de Ligt injury return for Manchester United
content:
Michael Carrick is uncertain when Manchester United defender Matthijs de Ligt will return from an injury absence.

The 26-year-old centre-back has not featured for United since the victory at Crystal Palace on November 30 with interim head coach Carrick saying he is dealing with a “back issue”.

De Ligt had featured in United’s first 14 matches of the season but has now missed three months of action.

“Matthijs has had a back issue which has been a bit slow to progress,” Carrick said on Friday. “It’s something we’ve been working through, he’s (going) in the right direction but a bit further behind.

“His timeframe? It’s the nature of the injury, the issue in the back, it’s a difficult one to pin down time-wise. He’s definitely improving.”

De Ligt has been involved with the Netherlands for two international squads this season and will be hopeful of returning to fitness ahead of this summer’s World Cup.

Carrick was more upbeat on a return to fitness for Mason Mount, who he says is “getting closer” to a return to availability having missed United’s last four matches.

“Mason is on the grass, he’s looking to be around it pretty soon,” Carrick said.

“We’ve had to be patient, he’s a good player, so we’re looking after him and making sure he’s ready for a big finish to the season.”

United, who have collected 16 points in six matches under Carrick, host Crystal Palace in the Premier League on Sunday.
